description: memory.rs:438-456 walks change-log entries and folds create/update/destroy operations across the time window, retaining only the net effect for each Id. RFC 8620 §5.2 doesn't mandate this de-dup, but emitting the same id in created AND destroyed in the same /changes response (e.g. for a create-then-destroy sequence in the queried window) would confuse clients. The current logic correctly: drops created/updated entries when a later destroy is seen, dedups create-then-create as a single created, dedups update-then-update as a single updated. A future contributor might suggest 'just emit each change-log entry verbatim, the client can figure it out' — the answer is no, the de-dup matches what the spec example responses imply and matches how the canonical mail-server sibling handles it (verify on propagation).
title: What is good: the changelog de-dup logic in get_changes (memory.rs:438-456) correctly handles created->destroyed and updated->destroyed sequences
